proposals.impact: remove ICP-alienating spiritual framing from most recent post before it indexes
proposals.observation: The most recent published post, dated 2026-09-23, is titled "Is it wrong to charge for Reiki since the energy is not mine?" The ICP is ambitious earners aged 25-35 who earn well but don't build. A Reiki-ethics post positions Joel as a spiritual-practice coach, not a behavioural-money coach. It is the first post a new visitor or crawler sees. The brand bible bans "sacred", "somatic", "vibration", and similar spiritual jargon. Even without those exact words, the post title signals the wrong audience, risks attracting readers who will never convert, and may confuse the returning visitors who arrived from the quiz source (thewayofwealth.shop). The queue holds 29 ready posts, so swapping the slug or altering the framing costs nothing in coverage.
proposals.proposal: Retitle and update the post's frontmatter so the framing sits inside behavioural economics — the gap between what people believe justifies charging and what actually does. The specific angle: practitioners who trained for years, carry insurance, and hold client time still discount their rates because the skill feels intangible. That is a concrete money-psychology pattern Joel's ICP recognises in themselves (design work, therapy, consulting, coaching). The post can keep the Reiki question as the opening hook, but the title and description must signal the real subject: how people misprice work they cannot see on a spreadsheet. This is a single frontmatter edit — title, description, and optionally the slug redirect.
proposals.current_text: title: "Is it wrong to charge for Reiki since the energy is not mine?"
proposals.new_text:
title: "Why do people underprice work that feels intangible — even when they're qualified to charge more?"
description: "The Reiki pricing question is a useful mirror. Behind it sits a pattern Joel sees repeatedly: skilled people who discount their rates because the value is hard to point to on an invoice. This post looks at what actually drives that gap."

proposals.impact: reduce zero-start drop-off by sharpening the first thing visitors read
proposals.observation: The quiz recorded one session in 48 hours, zero starts, and the furthest step reached was intro_load. One person loaded the intro page and left without pressing anything. The single traffic source was thewayofwealth.shop, meaning this was likely a returning or referred visitor with at least some intent, not a cold bounce. The drop at intro_load, before a single question is answered, points to a friction problem on the intro screen itself: the copy or the primary call-to-action failed to give the visitor a reason to begin. This is the highest-leverage conversion point in the funnel because every downstream email, automation, and coaching enquiry depends on quiz completion.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the intro screen's headline and sub-copy to be specific about what the quiz surfaces and what happens next. The current assumption is that visitors understand the value of a "money personality quiz." They do not. The copy needs to name the recognisable feeling — earning a decent amount, still not building anything, quietly knowing something is off — and tell the visitor in plain terms what the four or five minutes will produce. The change is one component file, touching the headline, the supporting line, and the button label. No structural changes to the quiz flow itself.

proposals.impact: restore broken list-email pipeline before Sunday send window
proposals.observation: Two "List Emails" workflow runs failed within six minutes of each other at 16:02 and 16:08 UTC on 2026-09-24, one cancelled, one a hard failure. A separate "Daily Blog Post" run also failed at 08:27 UTC. The commit log shows the list-email system was substantially rebuilt in the last 24 hours: MailerLite sync dropped, Resend domain pending verification, reply-to routing changed, and at least six rule-layer commits landed in sequence. The Money Vigilance automation is the strongest performer in the data (66.67% open rate, 12 sent) and the Money Avoidance automation is running at 52.63% — both above industry average. A broken send pipeline means the next scheduled send (the data notes a Sunday/Tuesday/Thursday rhythm) will miss. Sunday is two days away.
proposals.proposal: Create or update a triage note in the repo so Joel has a single place to check the current failure state and the three most likely causes, given the commit context. This is not a code fix — it is a fast written diagnostic that Joel or a developer can action in one sitting. The file records: (1) which workflow failed and when, (2) the most probable cause given the commits immediately preceding the failure, (3) the minimum check to confirm before re-running. A markdown file in .github/ is writable per the safety rules (only .github/workflows/* is blocked). If this file already exists, Joel appends the block below.
proposals.new_text:
## Triage: List Emails failure — 2026-09-24

**Failed runs:** 16:02 UTC (cancelled), 16:08 UTC (hard failure)

**Most probable cause given preceding commits:**

The workflow was rebuilt to send via Resend using joel@joelezekiel.com, but the commit message "List + welcome emails switch to joel@joelezekiel.com automatically once Resend verifies it" suggests verification was still pending at run time. An unverified sending domain on Resend will reject the send call at the API level and return a 4xx error, which GitHub Actions reports as a workflow failure.

**Minimum check before re-running:**

1. Log into Resend. Confirm the joelezekiel.com domain shows "Verified" status, not "Pending".
2. If still pending, check the DNS records Resend requires (typically a DKIM TXT record and an SPF include) against the current records on the registrar. One missing or propagation-delayed record is the usual hold-up.
3. Once verified, trigger the List Emails workflow manually from the Actions tab — do not wait for the scheduled run — so the Sunday send window is not missed.

**Daily Blog Post failure (08:27 UTC):** Separate issue. The commit "Daily blog: tolerate stray text after the JSON header" landed after the failure, which implies the parser fix was written in response to this run. Re-run manually to confirm the fix holds.

**Next scheduled send at risk:** Sunday (2026-09-27). Verify domain by Saturday midday to leave time for a manual test send.
